newsitem.title: LATVIA: THOMSON BOOSTS SOVEREIGN RATING TO BB+.
newsitem.headline: THOMSON BOOSTS SOVEREIGN RATING TO BB+.

text.p: Rating agency Thomson Bankwatch said on Tuesday that it has upgraded its sovereign rating for Latvia to BB+ from BB-, citing factors including government control of spending and falling interest rates and inflation.
An analyst for Thomson said the new rating was one notch below investment grade.

He quoted fellow analyst Betty Starkey as saying in a statement that the upgrade was made due to continued progress in economic reforms, the redirection of foreign trade to the West, especially to Germany and Sweden.
She also cited a steady fiscal performance with good budget discipline, a reform of the tax system and more privatisation.
Inflation and interest rates were also coming down and the 1996 budget deficit was below the target agreed with the International Monetary Fund (IMF), she added.
Starky also noted that Latvia's access to the international credit markets was improving.
Thomson's sovereign team recently visited the Baltic region and carried out the upgrade after the trip.
